answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the delta schedule in the umber ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the copper checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 246 aliases thus means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 17 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
